title: Observability, Logging & Debugging Agent Traces
why: Debugging multi-step autonomous agents is notoriously tricky because decisions are probabilistic. Structured logging allows you to inspect exact prompt payloads, model parameters, latency, and tool inputs/outputs.
objectives: Configure Python standard logging with structured formats
Log LLM prompt snapshots, token counts, and execution latency
Implement log rotation for production servers
concept: Never rely solely on print() statements. Proper logger levels (DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR) allow you to silence verbose prompt dumps in production while maintaining full trace visibility in staging.

code.content:
import logging
import time

logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format='%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s] [%(name)s]: %(message)s',
    handlers=[
        logging.StreamHandler(),
        logging.FileHandler('agent_traces.log', encoding='utf-8')
    ]
)
logger = logging.getLogger('AgentTracer')

def log_agent_step(step_num: int, model: str, prompt_tokens: int, duration_sec: float):
    logger.info(f'Step {step_num} | Model: {model} | Prompt Tokens: {prompt_tokens} | Latency: {duration_sec:.2f}s')

logger.info('Agent runner initialized.')
start = time.time()
time.sleep(0.5)  # simulate LLM latency
log_agent_step(1, 'gpt-4o', 320, time.time() - start)

practice.description: Create a decorator @trace_tool that logs tool execution time and input arguments automatically using logger.debug.

requirements: Output agent trajectory logs as JSON Lines (JSONL)

checklist: Configured dual console and file loggers
Recorded latency and token consumption metrics
mistakes: Logging sensitive API keys or unmasked PII into plain-text log files
